en: The Philippine eagle has a wingspan of up to 2 meters, making it the largest bird of prey in the Philippines.
The 1898 Declaration of Independence in Kawit, Cavite, marked the end of 333 years of Spanish colonial rule in the Philippines.
The Philippine Congress is bicameral, consisting of a 24-member Senate and a House of Representatives with over 300 lawmakers.
Although the Philippines has over 180 distinct languages, only Filipino and English are the two official languages of government.
The annual Sinulog Festival in Cebu attracts over 2 million tourists to celebrate the Santo Niño with grand street dancing.
Philippine national hero Jose Rizal was fluent in 22 languages, including Spanish, Latin, Greek, and Japanese, showcasing his exceptional intellect.
The indigenous Ifugao people built the Banaue Rice Terraces over 2,000 years ago, carving thousands of steps into mountains at elevations up to 1,500 meters.
The Sampaguita, the Philippine national flower, blooms year-round and produces small, fragrant white flowers measuring about 3 centimeters in diameter.
The 1987 Philippine Constitution, the current supreme law, contains exactly 18 articles detailing the government structure and bill of rights.
Dr. Ramon Barba invented a mango flowering technique that increased fruit yields by up to 300 percent, earning him National Scientist status.
Filipino citizens must be at least 18 years old to vote, and national elections for the president occur every 6 years.
The traditional Filipino bahay kubo is typically elevated 1 to 2 meters above the ground to protect inhabitants from floods and pests.
